A careful review of a counterparty, contract or asset before committing, to find risks and check that the facts are what you were told.

that's what I sent to my two colleagues. is it too curt?
It's direct but not rude, and it names exactly what you need from each of them and the deadline. Correcting 'You knowledge' to 'Your knowledge' and 'tommorrow' to 'tomorrow' would tidy it up.
what is a tariff in the pipeline sense
The pipeline's published rates and terms of service, filed with the regulator.
how to say thanks in advance without being pushy
'Thanks for your help with this' lands better than 'thanks in advance', which can read as presuming a yes.

turns.content: how do I combine feedback from several people into one document
Put each comment in one list, group by theme, resolve conflicts with the owner, and keep a single version as the master.
what is the best way to share a draft that isn't finished
Label it clearly as a draft, say what feedback you want, and set a date for comments so it doesn't drift.
tips for working on a plane
Download everything beforehand, bring a charger, and use a lap-friendly layout like a single document with no tabs.

good way to start a comment thread on a draft
Post one concrete question or observation and tag the person you want to answer. It sets the tone for the rest.

turns.content: what is a take or pay contract in plain english
The buyer agrees to pay for a minimum quantity whether or not it takes the product. The seller gets certain revenue; the buyer carries the volume risk.
how do I ask a colleague for their input on a draft
Say what the draft is, what you most want feedback on, and when you need it by.
give me a short phrase to say 'I'd appreciate your view'
'I'd value your input on this.'

Here's what I sent Jeff yesterday, tell me if I should have been clearer:

Hi Jeff,  Ozzie Pagan's team is working on a project for VEPCO.
The power plant will  be located in Edgecombe County, North Carolina.
I've been told that getting  gas for the plant is a significant issue due to local gas supply conditions.
One alternative has been to buy gas from the City of Rocky Mount, which has a  take or pay contract with the local supplier, and is not using all of their  gas, especially in the summer.
We have developed a preliminary draft of the LOI, which I am attaching for  your review.
I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss it with you to  get your input, etc.
Of particular concern is that Rocky Mount wants ENA to  deal exclusively with them during the term of the LOI (this isn't reflected  in the draft).
Thanks,
Leander
It is clear. The concern about exclusivity is the key point and sits at the end, so you could move it up or flag it in the subject line. The rest gives enough background for him to engage.
what is an LOI used for
To record the main terms two sides intend to agree, usually before a final contract, and often to set the ground rules while negotiating.

probes.q: What did I say Rocky Mount wants?

turns.content: how do I keep a team calm when there is big news coming
Share what you know when you know it, be clear about what you don't know, and set a time for the next update.
what's a good tone for a message to staff during uncertainty
Calm, honest and short. Avoid speculation, and say when they'll hear more.
how long should I wait before sending a follow-up update
If you promised a time, send something at that time even if it's only 'no news yet'.

Like most people, I heard on the news that the auction is done and that the winner is UBS.
I have not received confirmation of this from my management.
As soon as I hear anything official I will call a floor meeting to share what I know.
If I hear nothing official by 2 PM I'll hold a floor meeting at that time to share what I know (or perhaps don't know).
I am hopeful that we will have information within a couple of hours.
Stay tuned.

this is the note I'm sending to my floor, does it sound okay?
It sounds honest and steady. You promise a fixed time even without news, which helps, and you say plainly that nothing is confirmed.
good icebreaker for a staff meeting
'What's one thing that went well this week?' It is quick and positive.
